items.canonical_answer: Weathering breaks down or chemically alters rock in place, whereas erosion wears material away through a moving agent and removes it from its original position.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: weathering involves breakdown or chemical alteration.
1 mark: erosion wears a surface through a moving agent.
1 mark: make the difference in removal explicit: in-place change versus material taken away. Do not credit the same point twice.
items.provenance: Original structural exemplar; not a production-bank item.

items.prompt: Suggest why the observations support weathering at site A and erosion at site B. At A, a block has split and its fragments remain beneath it. At B, moving water carries fragments from an exposed face, which retreats. Use the given evidence.
items.canonical_answer: The split at A demonstrates breakdown, and the fragments remaining beneath the block show change in place. At B, moving water and the retreating face provide evidence of an active agent wearing away and removing material.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: apply the given split-block evidence to breakdown at A.
1 mark: use the fragments remaining as evidence of change in place.
1 mark: give the reason for erosion at B by linking the moving-water/retreat evidence to wearing away and removal.
items.provenance: Original structural exemplar; not a production-bank item.

items.prompt: Explain the error in this claim and give a test that distinguishes the processes: “A block has split, so that observation by itself proves erosion.”
items.canonical_answer: Splitting can demonstrate weathering in place; the claim does not establish wearing away and removal. Test whether a moving agent has worn and removed material, rather than inferring erosion from splitting alone.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: identify the confusion between rock breakdown and erosion.
1 mark: state the correct distinction and apply the test of evidence for a moving agent and removal.
